title: Process Optimization using High Throughput Automated Micro-Bioreactors in Chinese Hamster Ovary Cell Cultivation
protocol: Reconstitute recombinant CHO DG44 cells with 1.2 mL of cell suspension.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 15 mL conical centrifuge tube containing 10 mL of cold seed medium.
Centrifuge at 190 x g and room temperature for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Pre-heat 150 mL of seed medium in a 500 mL shake flask to 36.8 °C.
Gently resuspend the cell pellet in 10 mL of pre-warmed seed medium.
Transfer the cells into the shake flask.
Use 1 mL of sample from the flask to measure initial viable cell concentration and viability using a cell counter.
Incubate the shake flask in an orbital shaker at 36.8 °C, 7.5% CO2, with shaking rate of 120 rpm.
Take 1 mL of sample three days after passaging cells to measure final cell concentration.
Calculate volume to be transferred to fresh pre-warmed seed medium for initial cell concentration of 2 x 10^5 cells/mL in the new passage.
Passage cells 5 times in total before transferring to bioreactor.
Measure the final cell concentration of the preculture.
Calculate the volume to be transferred to achieve an initial cell concentration of 3 x 10^5 cells/mL in the bioreactor.
Fill the reactor with production medium a day before inoculation to equilibrate the reactor.
Set the process parameters including temperature at 36.8 °C and dissolved oxygen concentration (DO) at 60%.
Test stirrer speeds of 1050 rpm and 1300 rpm along with pHs of 6.9, 7.1, and 7.3.
Run the batch process for 72 hours after which feed medium is added every 24 h.
Create a new experiment in the AMBR cell culture software by clicking on Create New Experiment in the Introduction tab.
Enter the name of the experiment along with the date it is to be conducted in the New Experiment tab.
Activate the check point for the culture station and the vessels.
Activate Auto Add DOE Tags.
Click on Next to switch to the next tab.
Set information about addition of media, antifoam, inoculum, feed, and glucose.
Activate the Add Media Plate check point.
Define the plate type, name, and location containing the medium.
Depending on the type of plate and if it contains a lid, activate Is Lidded.
Click on Add Media To Vessels.
Enter the volume of media to be added into the vessels.
Define the mapping of transfer from the plate to the vessels.
Click on Next to switch to the next tab.
Set cultivation conditions in the reactor.
Assign temperature, target DO, upper pH limit, and stirring RPM (Up or Down stirring).
Activate Add Cell Plate.
Define the plate type, name, and location containing the medium.
Enter the time of inoculation.
Enter the volume of media to be added to the vessels.
Define the path travelled by the liquid handler from the plate to the vessels.
Deactivate Reuse Pipette Tips to prevent cross-contamination.
Set addition of feed.
Activate Add Feed Plate.
Define plate type, name, and location for the feed plate.
Enter volume of feed to be added to the vessels.
Define mapping of transfer of feed from the plate to the vessels.
Add number of feed additions as required by cultivation schedule.
Program feeding after 72 hours with subsequent feeds every 24 hours.
Manually enter time delay between feedings starting from initial inoculation.
Activate Add Sample Plate.
Define plate type, name, and location for sample plate.
Check on Take Sample from Vessels.
Enter the volume of the sample to be removed from the vessels.
Define the mapping of the transfer of the sample from the vessels to the plate.
Ensure that the volume does not decrease below 10 mL during cultivation.
Add the number of samples to be taken during cultivation.
Add the time of the sample being removed from the vessel for each input sample point.
Save the process.
Switch to the Process Steps tab in the AMBR cell culture software.
Select Process Step view to visualize the flow of the recipe.
Open the AMBR 15 DOE software and click on Investigation.
Select New to create a new DOE investigation.
Enter the name of the new DOE investigation in the Create Investigation dialog box.
Open the recipe created to study the different parameters.
Click on Browse and select the respective experiment.
Define the DOE factor.
Select the parameter and click on the column labeled DOE factor.
Select New to add units, abbreviation, lower and upper limit of the factors.
Define the response factor.
Define the response based on which the experimental analysis would be structured.
Click on Edit DOE Responses in the Responses tab.
Define the name, abbreviation, units, minimum and maximum limits for each response.
Select the AMBR variable for each response from the drop-down list.
Associate a micro-bioreactor variable with each response automatically if required.
Change the equation for each response to choose between minimum, maximum, first, last and average data.
Create a design using the Start Design Wizard.
Select the type of experimental design in the Start Design Wizard.
Add or remove the number of replicates and center points as needed.
Choose the objective: Screening, Optimization (RSM), or Split objective.
For Screening, use linear and interaction models to find important factors.
For Optimization (RSM), use quadratic and cubic models for detailed modeling and optimization.
Select the model and design along with the number of center points and replicates.
Click on Finish and switch to the next tab.
Create work packets using the AMBR cell culture software.
Import the created work packets into the AMBR control laptop.
In the Experiment tab, click Create DOE Experiment and browse for the imported work packet.
Click Start to initialize the process.
Export experimental results once the experiment is executed.
Open the Export DOE Results window and select desired rows from the table.
Click on Export Selected Rows or Export Experimental Data to save the results.
Import the data into the AMBR DOE module by switching to the Results tab and selecting Import Results.
Browse for the desired data file and click Analysis Results.
Analyze further in MODDE.
Open the gamma sterilized culture vessels under a laminar flow cabinet and orient in the culture station as depicted.
Clean the clamp plate with 70% ethanol and double distilled water.
Autoclave the cleaned clamp plate and place it on top of the vessel.
Mount the clamp plate with a stirrer plate, ensuring each pin is fixed firmly.
Tighten both the stirrer plate and clamp plate onto the stirring assembly.
Use the program written in Section 3 to run the cultivation.
Visualize the process steps scheduled or completed in the Process tab.
Pause the liquid handler when altering the cultivation steps during the process run.
Edit the process recipe after pausing the liquid handler as needed.
Add antifoam to the vessels before starting the stirrer to prevent excessive foaming during cultivation.
Fill the 24 well plate provided with the micro-bioreactors manually with sterile media.
Place the filled 24 well plate in the designated deck of the system according to the program.
Ensure the plate is placed in the correct deck designated by the written program.
Measure the viable cell concentration after the 5th passage.
Calculate the number of cells to be transferred to ensure an initial cell concentration of 3 x 10^5 cells/mL in all vessels.
Transfer 3.2 ml of cell suspension into each well of a 24 deep well plate for a required inoculum volume of 2 mL per vessel.
Place the 24 well plate on the designated deck.
Remove a 460 μL sample from the vessels every day using the liquid handler.
Dilute 200 μL of the daily sample with 800 μL of filtered 1x PBS buffer (5x dilution) and place in the cell counter.
Centrifuge the remaining sample for 5 min at 190 x g and room temperature, then store the supernatant for further analysis.
Freeze 100 μL of the supernatant at -20 °C until the end of cultivation for protein quantification.
Stop the monitoring of process parameters once they have terminated.
Unscrew the stirrer plate and clamp plate from the bioreactor.
Remove the culture vessels and clean the culture stations.
Place drying plates on the culture stations and screw them in.
Clean the clamp plates thoroughly with 70% ethanol and double distilled water.
Click on Stop in the bioreactor software once the drying cycle is completed.
Manually remove the content of the vessels into 50 mL centrifuge tubes on Day 12 of cultivation.
Centrifuge the cell broth at 190 x g for 30 min.
Discard the cell pellet and store the supernatant at -20 °C.
Prepare equilibration buffer as a solution of 0.5 M Na2HPO4 containing 0.5 M NaCl with pH 7.9.
Prepare elution buffer as a solution of 100 mM glycine containing 0.5 M NaCl with pH 2.
Filter both buffers through a 0.2 µm membrane and degas before analysis.
Purge the high-performance liquid chromatography system (HPLC) with freshly prepared equilibration buffer.
Load the protein A column onto the HPLC system for analysis.
Carry out chromatography with a flow rate of 1 mL/min.
Set the column oven temperature at 30 °C and autosampler temperature at 10 °C.
Thaw frozen samples at room temperature.
Filter 225 µL of each sample through a 0.22 µm PVDF membrane.
Dilute higher concentration protein samples in a 1:20 ratio with equilibration buffer.
Filter diluted samples through the membrane before placing in the autosampler.
Place the samples in the autosampler.
Load the method and sequence in the software.
Start the sequence.
